> 观自在菩萨，行深般若波罗蜜多时，照见五蕴皆空，度一切苦厄。

The sutra opens with a compound that has been flattened by two thousand years of recitation: 观自在.

*观* is not "look at". It is the capacity to see through — the observing that does not need an object to stand on. *自在* is not "free and easy" in the sense of leisure; it is unbounded, not tied. So the name is not a proper name at all. It is a description of a function: seeing that is not bound by what it sees.

The book is careful about this, and the carefulness matters, because the alternative reading — a Bodhisattva who is a person, somewhere, doing this — puts the whole sentence out of reach. If the capacity belongs to someone else, the sutra is biography. If it belongs to the mind, the sutra is an instruction.

## 行深 is not thinking harder

*行深* — practice deeply. The gloss in the book is exact: not shallow conjecture, not analysis, but abiding, maturing, entering this one act of seeing until it is present, not understood.

The distinction is one every reader has crossed without noticing. There is a version of this sentence where you sit and reason: form is impermanent, therefore form is empty, therefore my body is not me — a chain of correct inferences, each producing the next. That chain can be completed and leave you exactly where you were. 行深 says: this is not that.

## The cup

五蕴皆空: form, feeling, perception, formation, consciousness — all empty, in the technical sense of having no self-nature, no independent substance.

The book's image is a cup. Form is the bottom. Feeling, perception, formation and consciousness are the walls, raised around it. Conditions gather and the cup appears; conditions scatter and it is gone. The cup works — you can hold water in it — and there is no cup-substance anywhere in it. 有相可用，而无体可执.

That is what 空 means here, and the image earns its keep because it holds both halves at once. Empty is not "does not exist". Empty is "exists as a gathering".

## 度 as subtraction, not rescue

*度一切苦厄* — crosses over all suffering. The book refuses the rescue reading. 度, here, is what happens after the seeing: the place where suffering was attached has nothing left to attach to, and the binding loosens by itself.

Which is why the sentence order cannot be rearranged. Not: suffering, then rescue, then seeing. Seeing first, and the attachment dissolves because the thing it was gripping is no longer there.

## The test

Take one thing you are currently suffering about and locate the 蕴 it lives in. Is it a sensation in the body? A picture of a future? A sentence you keep repeating? Name it, then look for the cup-substance underneath it — the thing that would still be there if all the conditions were removed.

Most of the time there is nothing there, and the discovery is not comforting. That is the point at which 行深 begins to differ from analysis.
